page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.c5.xlarge is a compute-optimized virtual machine instance powered by the KVM hypervisor. It features an Intel Xeon 8163 processor with an x86_64 architecture, operating at a base frequency of 2.5 GHz. The instance is configured with 4 dedicated vCPUs derived from 2 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled. It includes 8.0 GB of system memory, yielding a resource density of 2.0 GB per vCPU. Local storage is not bundled with this instance, and network performance is rated at a baseline bandwidth of 2 Gbps.

Performance benchmarks place the ecs.c5.xlarge in the lower tiers of modern cloud compute resources. In stress-ng testing, the instance achieved a single-core CPU score of 1103.19 and a multi-core score of 2934.5, both falling into the bottom 25% of tested hardware. Memory bandwidth tests show a significant drop-off from cached small-block reads at 164.06 GB/sec to uncached large-block reads at 20.58 GB/sec, which is categorized in the bottom 10%. Similarly, Passmark CPU and memory scores of 3628.64 and 1246.19 respectively reflect weak to poor performance profiles.

Given its dedicated CPU allocation but lower-tier benchmark results, the ecs.c5.xlarge represents an entry-level compute-optimized option. It is qualitatively cost-efficient for workloads requiring dedicated CPU execution without demanding high memory throughput or massive parallel processing. Suitable workloads include lightweight web serving, basic Redis caching, small-scale software compilation, and low-intensity text or image processing tasks.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.c5.xlarge is an entry-level compute-optimized instance featuring 4 dedicated vCPUs and 8.0 GB of memory, powered by an Intel Xeon 8163 processor running at 2.5 GHz on the KVM hypervisor. Lacking local storage and integrated GPUs, it relies on network-attached storage and offers a baseline network bandwidth of 2 Gbps. Benchmark evaluations consistently place this instance in the bottom 25% for CPU and memory performance, with a single-core Geekbench score of 987.0 and a Passmark CPU score of 3628.64. Uncached memory bandwidth is limited, dropping to 20.58 GB/sec for large blocks. Given these performance characteristics, the ecs.c5.xlarge is best suited for lightweight, non-intensive workloads such as basic static web serving, minor Redis operations, and small-scale software compilation where dedicated CPU allocation is required but raw processing speed is not critical.
